findings: Anthropic review agrees that the durable layer is CI delegation to `ao-kernel quality check-changelog`; ADR-0005 semantics remain in the Python SSOT and do not drift into workflow YAML.

The workflow is fork-safe and read-only: it checks out the PR head SHA with fetch-depth:0, fetches the base ref for reproducible diffs, routes PR labels/body through env, and avoids pull_request_target or credential persistence.

The self-enforcement failure was correctly resolved by adding a `[Unreleased]` changelog bullet, not by relying on a label or weakening the gate. This keeps the new workflow compatible with its own policy on first landing.

Governance-sensitive surfaces are untouched: no CODEOWNERS, ruleset, branch protection, runtime live-adapter path, secret material, support widening, production claim, or live adapter execution mutation.
The shape tests cover workflow presence, permissions, CLI binding, local-hook coexistence, drift avoidance, and governance zero-touch invariants for the changelog enforcement lane.
